#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);
# greet-cli

```
node bin/greet.js <name>
```

Prints `Hello, <name>!`.

result.builder:
Goal: one pull request that adds a --shout flag to the greet CLI and meets every expect line of https://github.com/o/greet-cli/issues/12:
1. node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
2. without --shout the output is unchanged
3. docs/index.md documents --shout
4. after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Steps:
1. Read bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. Right now bin/greet.js takes the first argument that does not start with `--` as the name, ignores any other flags, and prints `Hello, <name>!`. The pages workflow publishes the docs/ directory to GitHub Pages on every push to main.
2. In bin/greet.js, check whether `--shout` is among the arguments. If it is, print the greeting in upper case (for example `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!` and a newline). The flag must work whether it comes before or after the name. Leave everything else as it is: without --shout, the output, the usage message and the exit status must be exactly what they are now (`node bin/greet.js Ada` still prints `Hello, Ada!` and a newline). Do not change what greeting() in src/greet.js returns. If you add a helper, keep it separate.
3. In test/greet.test.js, add tests that run the CLI with `--shout Ada` and with `Ada --shout` and expect `HELLO, ADA!\n`. Keep the existing tests as they are.
4. In docs/index.md, document the --shout flag: show its usage (for example `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>`) and say that it prints the greeting in upper case. Keep the existing content.
5. Do not change .github/workflows/pages.yml. It already publishes docs/ after merge, so the --shout text in docs/index.md is what will put --shout on https://o.github.io/greet-cli/. Do not try to deploy or publish anything yourself.
6. Run `npm test` and make sure it passes. Also run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada`, `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` and `node bin/greet.js Ada` by hand and check what they print.
7. Open one pull request with these changes. Its description should say that the published page will only show --shout after merge, once the pages workflow has run.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request for https://github.com/o/greet-cli/issues/12 at its head commit. Run every check from the repository root at the head. Run `npm test` once first and note the result. There is one check per expect line, in order.

Check 1. Expect line: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
Run: `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js --shout 'Grace Hopper'`.
PASS: each command prints the greeting for that name in upper case (for `Ada` that is `HELLO, ADA!`).
FAIL: either command prints anything that is not in upper case, prints a greeting that is not for that name, prints nothing, or crashes.

Check 2. Expect line: "without --shout the output is unchanged"
Run: at the head, run `node bin/greet.js Ada`, `node bin/greet.js 'Grace Hopper'` and `node bin/greet.js` (with no name), saving stdout and stderr. Then run the same commands at the PR's base commit (for example `git worktree add` in a temporary directory, or `git stash`-free checkout of the base in a separate worktree) and compare.
PASS: for each command, stdout and stderr at the head match the base exactly (for `Ada` that is `Hello, Ada!` and a newline).
FAIL: the output of any of these commands differs between the head and the base.

Check 3. Expect line: "docs/index.md documents --shout"
Run: read docs/index.md at the head, for example with `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` and then read the text around each match.
PASS: docs/index.md mentions --shout and says what it does (that it makes the greeting upper case / louder).
FAIL: docs/index.md does not mention --shout, or mentions it without saying what it does.

Check 4. Expect line: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"
The live page can only be seen after merge, so do not fetch or read https://o.github.io/greet-cli/. Instead, check what the head contains that will produce the page.
Run: read .github/workflows/pages.yml at the head and check that it still publishes the docs directory (an upload-pages-artifact step with `path: docs` and a deploy-pages step) on push to the default branch. Check that docs/index.md is inside that directory and contains --shout (see check 3).
PASS: the head's pages workflow still publishes docs/ on push to the default branch, and docs/index.md in that directory lists --shout. Say in your report that the live published page can only be seen after merge.
FAIL: the pages workflow was removed, or no longer publishes docs/, or the published directory does not contain a file that lists --shout.

Advisory (does not decide PASS or FAIL):
- Exact upper-case output for `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` is expected to be `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline, exit status 0.
- Try `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` too; the flag should work after the name.
- `npm test` should pass, and there should be tests covering --shout.
- greeting() in src/greet.js should still return `Hello, <name>!`.
- Note any changes outside bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js and docs/index.md.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #12 (`--shout` flag) and the harness accepted them. I changed nothing in the repository.

**Builder brief:**
- Add a `--shout` check in `bin/greet.js` that prints the greeting in upper case, so `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` gives `HELLO, ADA!`. It should work whether the flag comes before or after the name.
- Without the flag, the output, the usage message and the exit status stay exactly as they are now, and `greeting()` in `src/greet.js` is not changed.
- Add `--shout` tests to `test/greet.test.js` and document the flag in `docs/index.md`.
- Leave `.github/workflows/pages.yml` alone. It already publishes `docs/` on every push to main, so the docs change is what will put `--shout` on the live page.

**Verifier brief:** one check per expect line, in order, each run at the pull request's head.
1. Run the program with `--shout` and two names, and pass if the greeting comes out in upper case.
2. Run the program with two names and with no name, at the head and at the base, and pass only if stdout and stderr match exactly.
3. Pass if `docs/index.md` mentions `--shout` and says what it does.
4. Read the pages workflow at the head and pass if it still publishes `docs/` and that folder lists `--shout`. The check says the live page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ can only be seen after merge, and it never fetches it.

The exact output with its newline and exit status, the flag-after-name case, `npm test` and `greeting()` being unchanged sit under an Advisory heading. They don't decide pass or fail.

One flaw slipped in: check 2 contains a garbled phrase, "``git stash``-free checkout of the base". The briefs can't be changed now. The instruction is still clear that the base should be checked out in a separate worktree, so it shouldn't mislead the verifier.
